decisions.executionNote: Approach blue nut with left arm and red nut with right, gradually turning downward while keeping elbow-up continuity; estimated nut locations from head RGB.
Finish vertical alignment over the blue and red nuts, lowering to a pregrasp height. Check wrist centering before closure.
Small wrist-based blue centering adjustment, descend to nut grasp height, close both grippers, and lift slightly to verify retention from RGB.
Both nuts appear retained. Lift clear, carry each over its matching upright screw within the same arm workspace, then approach from above.
Use wrist lateral offsets to center nuts over shafts, then lower gently to the thread-entry height and inspect alignment before tightening.
Refine shaft centering, seat both nuts gently, and begin a controlled clockwise tightening stroke while holding closed.
Settle the nuts further onto the shafts, with a small red centering correction. Open and reset wrist angles for another tightening stroke.
Regrasp both nuts and apply a slow clockwise stroke with a small downward thread-following motion; red seating remains less certain.
Red cap appears near flush, so release and lift clear for inspection. Reset the left wrist and regrasp blue slightly lower for further tightening.
Continue a measured blue tightening stroke, keeping closed. Red remains upright after release; move the right arm back toward its home corridor.
Reset and regrasp blue for a careful alignment check; its depth is not yet visually convincing. Finish returning the empty right arm home.
Blue shaft remains visible inside the nut. Continue another controlled clockwise turn with gentle axial descent; keep the right arm parked.
Corrected tensor; prior rejected call moved nothing. Release blue, lift clear, reset wrist and begin moving toward the central gray nut.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller wrist increments. Blue remains upright after release; approach the gray nut from the left at clearance height.
Align the left gripper over the central gray nut and descend to a pregrasp height, keeping the right arm parked and both elbows continuous.
Use the wrist view to center on gray, close at nut height, and lift a few centimeters to verify retention before transport.
Gray is visible between the fingers after lifting. Raise for clearance and carry it left over the matching gray screw, keeping the grasp closed.
The gray shaft is left of the held nut in the wrist view. Apply a small lateral correction and descend slowly to inspect thread entry.
Refine gray alignment at the lower height: the shaft now appears right of the opening. Correct a few millimeters and lower to thread-entry height without twisting yet.
Gray is laterally centered but its engagement is uncertain. Apply a slow clockwise stroke with very small axial descent, then inspect the shaft inside the opening.
The gray shaft is visible inside the nut after turning. Release to reset the wrist without backing off the nut, then regrasp for further tightening.
Reclose on gray and continue clockwise tightening with a small downward thread-following motion, maintaining the same alignment.
Gray remains aligned but not visibly deep enough. Open and reset the wrist without axial motion, then regrasp for another tightening pass.
Continue a controlled clockwise gray tightening stroke, following the thread only slightly downward. Keep the right arm parked and inspect depth afterward.
Release and reset the left wrist, then regrasp gray for a final measured tightening pass. Keep the nut height unchanged during the reset.
Apply another slow clockwise gray stroke with gentle axial following; the shaft is visible but final seating is not yet certain.
Release gray and lift clear to inspect whether it stays seated. Begin a small empty-hand retreat and wrist reset without disturbing the assembled pairs.
Gray stays upright with its shaft near the opening after release. Blue appears less deeply seated, so approach it again for a visual regrasp and additional tightening.
Blue is centered under the gripper with the shaft still recessed. Regrasp at this height and tighten clockwise with minimal downward motion to avoid tilting it.
Reset the blue grip for additional tightening rather than assuming completion. Bring the right arm back above red, with small continuous elbow-up motions, for a final fastening check.
The close right-wrist view shows red nearly flush, so leave it undisturbed and return that arm. Tighten blue further with a slightly larger but gradual downward follow.
Reset blue without reverse-driving the nut, regrasp slightly lower, and place the empty right arm at its starting pose. Blue still needs a seating check.
Let the blue grasp settle, then apply a further clockwise tightening stroke with a small axial follow. Leave the other pairs undisturbed.
Release blue and lift away to inspect its unsupported seating. Reset the empty left wrist while leaving all three color-matched pairs undisturbed.
All three pairs remain upright after release. Begin returning the empty left arm toward its origin, resetting yaw in small increments above the objects.
Return the empty left arm along its own workspace toward the starting pose, gradually restoring orientation while maintaining configuration continuity and open grippers.
Finish returning both empty arms to their initial EE poses and hold with grippers open. The matched pairs remain upright; final fastening depth is judged only from RGB.
The blue shaft remains visibly recessed, so return the left arm for further tightening rather than infer completion from upright placement. Keep the right arm home.
Finish the downward gripper orientation and approach blue at its current seated height. Inspect centering before regrasping.
Correct the blue nut's small wrist-image offset before closure, then tighten clockwise while following down only a few millimeters.
Release blue after the additional tightening and lift clear. Reset the empty wrist and retreat slightly, checking that all matched pairs remain upright without support.

Finish the return to both starting EE poses and hold with open grippers, leaving the three upright matched assemblies undisturbed.
Return above gray and red for close inspection and any remaining tightening. Approach within each arm's own workspace with open grippers and continuous elbow-up motion.

Regrasp gray and make another measured clockwise tightening pass with a small axial follow. Correct the empty right arm to its starting pose.
Release gray and withdraw vertically before retreating. Inspect the unsupported assemblies and return with both grippers open rather than relying on tracking as proof of fastening.
Gray remains upright and nearly flush after release. Return the empty left arm to its origin with open grippers and gradual orientation restoration.
Blue still has visibly exposed internal threads above the shaft. Reapproach it for a better-centered tightening grasp, leaving the flush gray and red pairs untouched.
Center the gripper on blue at a slightly higher grasp height, finish the vertical orientation, and let closure settle before applying torque.
Turn blue clockwise from the settled higher grasp, keeping axial motion very small so the nut can follow its thread without being pushed sideways.
Release blue, reset the wrist without driving the nut backward, and lower the open gripper slightly to regrasp at the nut's seated height.
Blue is slightly right of the wrist grasp center. Recenter the open fingers laterally, then let a closed grasp settle without changing height or twisting.
Blue is now centered between the fingers. Tighten clockwise with gradual axial following, retaining the closed grasp and leaving gray and red untouched.

The home wrist view still shows a recessed blue shaft. Reapproach with a different grasp yaw to allow a longer uninterrupted tightening stroke, keeping gray and red untouched.
Descend over blue with a small wrist-based centering correction and close at the seated nut height. This yaw leaves more wrist travel for tightening.
Use the available wrist travel for a longer continuous clockwise blue tightening stroke, following the thread downward gradually while retaining the grasp.
Complete a small remaining clockwise turn, release blue, and lift vertically clear before resetting the empty wrist. Inspect unsupported seating without disturbing the other pairs.
Blue stays upright after release with the shaft near the opening. Retreat the empty left arm and reset its wrist above the table; restore the right arm's origin pose.
Finish the empty left arm's return to its initial pose with gradual rotation and open grippers. Leave the three upright matched assemblies undisturbed.
